playbooks.why: ad/GOAD-Mini has its OWN entry in the fork's top-level playbooks.yml, so this tier must not fall through to `default:` — that chain runs ad-child_domain.yml and ad-trusts.yml against empty groups.

kept: data/inventory group layout and host-key membership, verbatim
providers/proxmox/inventory host -> {{ip_range}}.N -> dict_key mapping, octets unchanged
data/config.json hosts: hostname / type / domain / path / local_admin_password (values replaced with generic placeholders)
data/config.json domains: dc / netbios_name / domain_password / laps_path / trust (values replaced with generic placeholders)
stripped: domains[*].groups — emptied to {} (upstream carries the universal/global/domainlocal scope buckets; the composer must re-emit all three, roles/ad indexes ad_groups.global with no default)
domains[*].gmsa — emptied to {} (absent on this tier upstream; carried as an empty object so every tier has one shape)
hosts[*].vulns / vulns_vars — emptied ([] / {}); upstream dc01 planted disable_firewall, directory, files and adcs_templates
hosts[*].security / security_vars — emptied ([] / {}); upstream dc01 planted account_is_sensitive
hosts[*].local_groups — emptied to {}; every upstream entry named a domain user or group, i.e. payload
files/ — dropped entirely (upstream shipped files/dc01/templates/ESC1.json for the adcs_templates role)
README.md — dropped; provenance lives in this file
data/inventory_disable_vagrant — dropped; only data/inventory is a chassis input
providers/{aws,azure,ludus,virtualbox,vmware,vmware_esxi} and every *.tf — dropped; the lane provider is proxmox
composer_must_fill: domains[*].users and domains[*].groups — goad-preflight REQUIRED_DOMAIN_KEYS lists both; ansible/ad-data.yml reads lab.domains[d].users and .groups with NO `| default(...)`
domains[*].organisation_units if any users[*].path or groups[*][*].path names an OU
the placeholder identifiers below — every one is deliberately implausible so a leak is unmistakable rather than believable

placeholders.why: .invalid is the RFC 2606 reserved TLD, so a chassis domain that survives into a generated lab cannot be mistaken for a client's.

note: A CHASSIS IS DELIBERATELY NOT DEPLOYABLE. It is compile-time INPUT read on the orchestrator, not a lab: the compiler repopulates it and emits ad/CIAB-<hash>/, which is pushed to the controller separately. The controller never reads a chassis. Deploying one as-is dies in ad-data.yml, which dereferences lab.domains[d].users and .groups with no default — a domain whose groups are empty kills that play. That is correct and expected. Re-syncing when upstream moves is a mechanical diff: point at the same paths under the goad_ref above, re-apply the `stripped` list, and re-run front-end/test/ciab-chassis.test.js.
